conventions.convention: Strict convexity uses the outward normal and g(∇w νout,w)>0. Simplicity means strict convexity, no conjugate points, and nontrapping; dimension is at least two.
R(X,Y)Z=∇X∇YZ−∇Y∇XZ−∇[X,Y]Z, and Jacobi fields satisfy Dt²J+R(J,γ̇)γ̇=0.
The wave operator is ∂t²−Δg+q with Δg=divg∇g. Complex Hilbert inner products are linear in the first argument.

Forward waves have zero initial data, terminal waves have zero terminal data, and both DN maps return the outward normal derivative. Boundary inputs belong to Cc∞((0,T)×∂M); Green pairings are bilinear without conjugation.
The ray-integral theorem concerns real static interior potentials and maximal rays of strictly positive length L<T. Surface uniqueness assumes a finite uniform length bound L* and T>L*.

Gaussian beams use Dj=−i∂xj and ιHp ωcan=dp. General operators have a transported weight; weight one is asserted for real self-adjoint waves in physical time with |∂tφ|=1 and initial mass one. Endpoint residuals are excluded explicitly.
Finite-union jet realization requires full ambient Whitney remainder compatibility, not merely matching jets at intersections; parameter families also require uniform remainder moduli.
Finite-time invisibility uses intrinsic distance and the strict condition d(supp(q1−q2),∂M)>T/2.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary and smooth real static potential, homogeneous Dirichlet waves have a unique energy solution for initial data in H0¹×L² and forcing in L¹tL²x, with the stated uniform energy estimate. Terminal solvability follows by time reversal; smooth time-compact boundary data admit classical solutions by lifting and the proved regularity bootstrap.

Assume Countable Choice. For a compact connected simple background and any boundary point x0, the exponential map from inward vectors of lengths strictly between zero and their first exit times is a diffeomorphism onto M°. Each interior point has a unique minimizing geodesic from x0, and its distance function is smooth with unit gradient.

Assume Countable Choice. For real smooth interior potentials on a simple background, a maximal unit-speed ray of length 0<L<T and a shift 0<t0<T−L admit exact forward and terminal waves whose normalized product converges to integration along (t0+s,γ(s)); the correction remainders have the displayed energy bound and L² order O(λ⁻¹ᐟ²).
For the stated classical forward q1 wave u and terminal q2 wave v, the integral of (q1−q2)uv over Q equals the boundary integral of kΛq1⁺h−hΛq2⁻k, paired bilinearly with outward normal traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Equal full forward wave DN maps for real static Cc∞(M°) potentials on a simple background imply that the integral of q1−q2 over every inward-to-outward boundary geodesic with interior otherwise and length 0<L<T is zero.

On a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, the stated space-time Green identity holds for C² functions; every smooth time-compact boundary input has a smooth collar lift with a C¹ bound, and the classical normal trace has the stated L² bound.

Homogeneous-boundary waves propagate no faster than unit intrinsic speed; waves with zero initial data and boundary input starting at s0 vanish where distance to the boundary exceeds t−s0. The backward assertion also holds. Consequently the forward-terminal interior potential pairing vanishes when the nonempty difference support has distance greater than T/2 from the boundary.

All-order continuous jets on a compact Euclidean set satisfying full uniform Whitney compatibility admit a choice-free smooth extension. Uniform coefficient bounds and remainder moduli on a fixed compact set yield uniformly bounded extension seminorms on compact sets.
